title: Method: one network for every decision, behaviour cloning then PPO with a league
text: Third method, deliberately unlike the GA (evolved rules) and az-v1 (tree search over buys): a 298-256-256-34 MLP answers all ~22 kinds of decision, imitates the GA genome first (1.08 M decisions, 98.5% agreement), then improves by PPO (clip 0.2, GAE lambda 0.95, entropy 0.01) against 40% GA base, 15% bots, 15% past snapshots, 30% itself. Runs in C inside the engine: 3 ms per game, so 3,000 games per ~10 s iteration.
rejected: more search (az-v1 showed it saturates); evolution again; a value-only method (DQN) — PPO is the standard, stable choice for a large discrete action space with masking

title: Iteration 100: level with az-v1's best agent after 25 minutes of RL
text: Goal checks against the GA base (az-v1's 1,000 goal games): 59.6% (iteration 25), 63.6% (50), 65.3% (75), 67.3% (100); the imitating network started at 52% in the evaluation games. Head to head against az-v1's best agent (net 357 + 400-simulation search, 1,000 fresh games): 49.2% (46.1-52.3%). The bot scores slid from 74.8% to 71.5%: it specialises against the GA genome, its most frequent opponent.

title: Built the AZ seat check: az-v1's best agent scores 69.7% on the same 1,000 goal games inside this engine build (az-v1 measured 70.2%), so the two projects' numbers compare directly.
Run r1 stopped at iteration 203: level with az-v1's best, no longer climbing
text: Goal checks vs the GA base: 67.3% (100), 66.4% (125), 68.0% (150), 67.2% (175), 68.4% (200). Head to head vs az-v1's best: 49.2% (100), 49.4% (200). Bots recovered to 76.8%. The league never contains the agent to beat.

title: Run r2: az-v1's agent joins the league
text: From r1's newest net. League: 30% GA base, 15% bots, 15% past snapshots, 15% az-v1's best net without search (its buys, GA actions; fast), 5% az-v1's best agent with 400-simulation search (~0.5 s a game), 20% itself. Head-to-head checks every 50 iterations.
rejected: keeping r1's league (flat at ~68% / ~49% for 100 iterations)

title: r2 iteration 50: first win head to head against az-v1's best
text: 1,000 fresh games against az-v1's best agent (net 357 + 400-simulation search): 54.3% (51.2-57.3%), the whole interval above 50%. Against the GA base on az-v1's goal games: 68.0% (az-v1's best: 69.7% on the same games); bots 78.3%. In training (sampling) it scores ~52-55% against az-v1's net and ~52-58% against its search. Half of the goal is met; the other half (above 70% vs the GA) not yet.

title: Confirmed: rl-v1 is better than az-v1's best agent
text: Model models/rl_r2_200 (r2 iteration 200), on games never used anywhere: head to head against az-v1's best agent (net 357 + 400-simulation search) 55.0% of 2,000 games (52.8-57.1%); against the GA base 70.3% of 2,000 new games (68.2-72.2%), where az-v1's best scores 69.0% on the very same games. On az-v1's goal games: 70.6% vs the GA base (az-v1's best 69.7%), 80.1% vs the three bots (75.6%). Goal checks along r2: head to head 54.3% / 55.4% / 54.6% / 54.6% at iterations 50 / 100 / 150 / 200; vs GA 68.0% → 70.6%.

title: Release: models/rl_r2_200
text: r2's net 200, confirmed on 4,000 new games, saved as models/rl_r2_200.npy (+ .pt). Chosen at a goal-check iteration, before the confirmation, so the confirmation numbers are not selected.
rejected: a later or best-evaluation checkpoint (selection by evaluation would flatter it)
